previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and constipation. She had severe epigastric pain radiating to the right side, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, with no relief from her usual oral Dilaudid. Labs showed leukocytosis and mild metabolic abnormalities. Imaging confirmed appropriate GJ tube placement without obstruction. She was treated with IV fluids, pain control using scheduled IV Dilaudid, and initiation of oral naloxone for opioid-induced constipation, which led to a successful bowel movement. She advanced to clear liquids and tolerated tube feeds. A Code Purple occurred when she attempted to take unauthorized pills, leading to sedation with Ativan and Zyprexa. Antibiotics for mild G-tube site erythema were discontinued after reassessment. Her insulin regimen was continued without change. She was discharged home with an aggressive bowel regimen, clear instructions on pain management, and follow-up plans.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ yo female with a h/o DMI, chronic

and borderline personality disorder presents with abdominal 
pain, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea.

# Abdominal Pain, n/v, diarrhea: Perhaps related to chronic 
pancreaitis flare (but reassuring lipase wnl), or 
diabetes-induced gastroparesis. Given reported diarrhea and 
fever, infectious (viral/bacterial) gastroenteritis is also a 
possibility, but her lack of leukocytosis makes this less 
likely, and no diarrhea/stool sample or vomiting documented 
during hospitalization. Given recent URI could be post-viral 
IBS. Could also be pain-med seeking given many recent 
hospitalizations.
With treatment with IV pain regimen of 1mg IV dilaudid q3h prn, 
with IV compazine 10mg q6h prn, home PPI, home remeron, holding 
tubefeeds, home metoclopramide, benadryl PO qhs only, NPO, and 
IVF, pain, n/v, diarrhea all improved. At the time of discharge, 
the patient was tolerating a regular diabetic diet, and was able 
to have her nausea and pain controlled on po medications only.

had to negotiate how frequently to give it. mood seemed stable. 
patient initially refused PO meds, but eventually became willing 
to comply with an oral medication regimen.
